weaknesses: Higher monthly fees compared to online-only competitors
Strict balance requirements to waive fees
In-person application requirements for some loan products
Longer underwriting timelines compared to fintech lenders
Limited business savings account interest rates
Complex fee structures on some products
High annual fees on premium credit cards

Faster approval processes by fintechs (hours vs. days/weeks for banks)
Alternative credit assessment models (cash flow analysis vs. credit scores)
Lower operational costs enable competitive pricing
Superior user experience and mobile-first design
Specialized vertical solutions for specific industries
However: Chase charging fintech firms for data access shifts power dynamic back to banks
competitive_response: Signed data access agreements with major fintechs, charging for API access
Launched digital-first products like Tap to Pay on iPhone
Invested heavily in AI and automation to match fintech speed
Enhanced digital banking platforms to #1 rankings
Maintained branch network as competitive advantage for deposits and trust
Leveraged scale to offer competitive merchant services pricing
Built fintech partnership ecosystem rather than pure competition
